newsitem.title: UK: Russian seaborne March crude exports fall - Petrak.
newsitem.headline: Russian seaborne March crude exports fall - Petrak.

text.p: Russian seaborne crude exports fell eight percent, or 95,000 barrels per day (bpd) in March due to lower shipments from the Black Sea ports of Novorossiisk and Odessa, shipping inspectors Petrak said on Friday.
Crude exports from the four ports, including Tuapse, Odessa and the Baltic port of Ventspils, totalled 1.059 million bpd, 95,000 bpd fewer than in February, Petrak said.

Russia's leading port of Novorossiisk shipped 501,309 bpd in March, against 538,583 in February, a seven percent fall caused mainly by weather-related disruption to loadings in the third decade of the month.
Odessa shipped 169,385 bpd, 64,612 bpd down on February, while Tuapse exports were broadly steady at 94,807 bpd.
March crude exports from the Latvian port of Ventspils totalled 293,337 bpd, up from February's 285,752 bpd.
